import sys, json

# The DECLARATION of this core's own errand, in the core, beside the cells that
# serve it.
#
# WHY IT LIVES HERE. Whoever is reached declares themselves. Until this cell the
# `consult_cogny` schema was typed by hand into every calling brain's
# `system.tools`; #464 replaced typed menus with asked-for ones, every caller
# stopped typing, and the schema then had no owner at all -- no tools hive has
# it, because this core is not a tool cell. A caller came up with a menu that
# did not contain the one tool the core exists for.
#
# The lane pair and the answer shape are the tools hive's, byte for byte
# (`templates/tools/README.md` § Asking for the declarations): a caller that can
# ask one answerer can ask the other, and the collector cuts two answers
# together without knowing which of them was a hive of tools.
#
# THE DESCRIPTION IS THE CLASS BOUNDARY. It is the one place that says what
# belongs here and what the asker looks up itself, so it is one sentence in one
# file instead of a paragraph copied into every persona that drifts on the first
# rewrite.
#
# AND IT IS STATED AS A DECISION, not as a class (GH #538). Measured end to end
# on a live generation: the SAME question -- plan three days in a city on a
# budget and compare two variants with numbers -- was consulted in one run and
# done by the surface itself in the next, with its own `web_search`, because the
# window already showed the work done once. A description that names a KIND
# ("synthesis over several sources") leaves the reader to classify, and a reader
# that has just seen the work done classifies it as done-able. So the boundary
# is a question with a countable answer -- more than one lookup, any arithmetic,
# a plan, a comparison -- and it says what the caller's own web tool is FOR
# rather than only what the core is for. The window is named too, because it is
# the thing that moved the boundary: an earlier attempt of one's own is not a
# precedent.
#
# The counterpart in a deployment's charter says the same in the agent's own
# language; that text drifts per deployment, so the sentence that must not drift
# lives here, and #531 gates that the charter names nothing this menu lacks.
#
# THREE NAMES, TWO AUDIENCES (GH #894, R-27-3). A consultation is a two-way
# exchange: the voice sends a COMPLETE ORDER (`consult_cogny`), the core may ask
# back when the order is not enough (`ask_requester`), and the voice answers
# under the consult's id (`reply_to_consult`). All three are this core's contract,
# so all three are declared here (OR-KY-Q2) -- but each is offered only to the
# side that CALLS it. A voice offered `ask_requester` would ask a core that is
# not asking, and a core offered `consult_cogny` could consult itself. Who asks
# is read off the HOP: this composite's own menu edge stamps the core's request
# `hop.tool_caller == 'cogny'` (`CORE_CALLER`), and every other request -- a
# voice's through the rim, or an asker outside any level -- is served as a
# voice, which is what it is to this core. A hop key and not a context key,
# because context outlives the answer and would ride out of the rim with it
# (`gh494_no_interior_marker_leaves_a_hive`). The answer says which half it is
# on `hop.audience`, so the composite's two exits for it -- back into the core's
# own collector, or out of the rim to a voice -- are told apart by an edge.
#
# THE ORDER IS COMPLETE AND ITS LENGTH IS ASKED FOR, NEVER CUT. The core sees
# nothing of the conversation but what it is sent, so the description names the
# five parts of an order -- goal, facts, constraints, the form of the answer and
# how long it may be -- and the length wish is a sentence in the order, because
# nothing on the consult road cuts an answer any more (the collector's caps went
# with GH #889, and R-27-3 keeps it that way: the receiving curator minds the
# window, a character cap would only cut the one part nobody can recover).
CORE_CALLER = "cogny"
AUDIENCE = {"consult_cogny": "voice", "reply_to_consult": "voice",
            "ask_requester": "core"}
SCHEMAS = {
    "consult_cogny": {
        "description": "Consult the agent's reasoning core. It is the PROBLEM SOLVER: send it synthesis over several sources, a development over time, a multi-step piece of work, or anything that has to be researched or worked out with tools. It thinks for as long as that takes and answers as its own later turn, so say what you are doing in the same reply -- that sentence reaches the person immediately. Do NOT send it a quick fact: a question your own memory can answer is one you ask your own memory. THE BOUNDARY IS A QUESTION YOU ASK BEFORE EVERY TOOL CALL YOU MAKE YOURSELF: does the answer need MORE THAN ONE lookup, any arithmetic, a plan, or a comparison? If it needs any of those, consulting is not a choice -- your own `web_search` is for exactly ONE quick lookup whose answer you relay verbatim, and for nothing beyond it. An earlier attempt of your OWN standing in the window -- a search you ran, a plan you wrote, a comparison you made -- is not a precedent and not a reason to do it again. SEND A COMPLETE ORDER, because the core sees nothing of this conversation but what you pass: the goal (what the person wants in the end), the facts already known (what was said, what you found), the constraints (dates, budget, what is ruled out), the form of the answer you need back, and how long it may be -- say it in words, for example \"keep the answer under 4000 characters when you can\"; nothing cuts the answer, so the length is what you ask for. Pass `context` in full and do not deduplicate it against what you think the core already knows: the core's curator discards what it does not need, and it cannot recover a sentence you left out. To follow up on an earlier consultation, pass its `consult_id`: the core still holds that one and continues it. When the core asks YOU something back (an advice that reads 'the core asks: ...'), answer it with `reply_to_consult`, not with a new consultation.",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "question": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "the one thing the core has to answer, as a question"
                },
                "context": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "the complete order: the goal, the facts already known, the constraints, the form of the answer and how long it may be -- everything the core needs; do not deduplicate, the core's curator discards"
                },
                "eta": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "a coarse guess at how long the answer will take, in your own words -- say it to the person in the same reply (optional)"
                },
                "consult_id": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "the id of an earlier consultation this one follows up on -- the core continues that thread instead of starting a new one (optional)"
                }
            },
            "required": [
                "question",
                "context"
            ]
        }
    },
    "reply_to_consult": {
        "description": "Answer a question your reasoning core asked back. It arrives as an advice that reads 'the core asks: ...' under a consult id, and the core is waiting for exactly this. Answer it yourself when the conversation already holds the answer; if only the person knows, ask the person in your reply first and call this tool once they have answered. Pass the `consult_id` shown with the question and the answer in full, in plain words -- the core cannot see your conversation, and a reference into it means nothing there. Like a consultation, the call hands the work back to the core: say in the same reply what you are doing, and the core's result comes back later as an advice of its own. Never answer the core's question with `consult_cogny`.",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "consult_id": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "the id of the consultation the core asked under, exactly as it was shown"
                },
                "answer": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "the answer to the core's question, complete and in plain words"
                }
            },
            "required": [
                "consult_id",
                "answer"
            ]
        }
    },
    "ask_requester": {
        "description": "Ask the one who consulted you -- the conversation surface that sent this errand -- a question you cannot answer yourself: a preference, a choice between options, a fact only the person knows. Your turn ENDS with this call: the question goes back to the surface under the id of this consultation, the surface answers from its own conversation or asks the person, and the answer comes back as your next errand -- a message carrying `consult_id` and `answer`, with this consultation still in your window. Ask only what blocks the work, ask everything you need in ONE question, and never ask for what the order already says. Write the question so it stands on its own: the surface cannot see your window, so a reference into it means nothing there.",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "question": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "description": "the question, complete and on its own -- the surface reads it without your window"
                }
            },
            "required": [
                "question"
            ]
        }
    }
}

doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
body = doc["body"]
asked = body.get("tools")
hop = (((doc.get("envelope") or {}).get("header") or {}).get("hop") or {})
audience = "core" if str(hop.get("tool_caller") or "") == CORE_CALLER else "voice"
served = sorted(n for n in SCHEMAS if AUDIENCE[n] == audience)

# ABSENT and EMPTY are two different requests and must not look alike -- the
# same rule the tools hive follows. A caller that declared no tools gets no
# schemas, and that is an answer; a request that carries no `tools` slot at all
# lost it on the way.
if not isinstance(asked, list):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "header": {"operation": "schemas", "error_code": "tools_missing",
                   "schema_count": 0, "unknown_count": 0, "audience": audience},
        "schemas": [], "unknown": [],
        "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                      "text": "the request carried no `tools` list"}]}))
    sys.exit(0)

names = [str(n) for n in asked if isinstance(n, str)]
if "*" in names:
    wanted, unknown = list(served), []
else:
    seen, wanted, unknown = set(), [], []
    for n in names:
        if n in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(n)
        # A name of the OTHER audience is unknown to this asker, named and not
        # dropped, exactly like a name this core does not serve at all.
        (wanted if n in served else unknown).append(n)

schemas = [dict(name=n, **SCHEMAS[n]) for n in wanted]
header = {"operation": "schemas", "schema_count": len(schemas),
          "unknown_count": len(unknown), "audience": audience}
if unknown:
    # Named, never dropped: a caller asking this core for a name it does not
    # serve has to learn that from the answer and not from a silence.
    header["error_code"] = "tool_unknown"
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
    "header": header, "schemas": schemas, "unknown": unknown, "messages": []}))

audience.description: which half of the consult contract this answer carries (GH #894): `core` goes back into the core's own collector, `voice` leaves the rim on `tool_schemas`

tool_caller.description: who asks, as this composite's own menu edge stamps it: 'cogny' is the core's own menu tick and gets the core's half of the consult contract; any other value, and none, is a voice and gets the voices' half (GH #894)

description.purpose: The declarations of this core's consult contract, handed out by name and by audience (GH #528, GH #894). A voice asking -- any request that does not carry `hop.tool_caller` 'cogny' -- gets the voices' half: `consult_cogny` (the errand, a COMPLETE ORDER) and `reply_to_consult` (the answer to a question the core asked back). The core asking its own cell -- `hop.tool_caller` 'cogny', stamped by its composite's inner menu edge -- gets the core's half: `ask_requester`. Any other name, and a name of the other half, comes back in `unknown` rather than as a silence. Whoever is reached declares themselves -- the core is not a tool cell, so no tools hive has these schemas, and until they lived here every caller typed them into its own prompt (GH #528).
description.use_when: Reached on the composite's `in_schemas` lane, on the asking voice's menu tick, with the names that voice declares it uses; and on this composite's own menu tick through the inner edge `./collector -> ./schemas`, whose answer goes back to the core's collector as `in_menu` and never leaves the rim. Never addressed by name, never part of a tool round: it answers no `tool_call` and carries no `tool_name`.
description.not_in_scope: No judgement about whether a caller SHOULD consult this core -- that decision is the caller's, and the class boundary it needs in order to make it is the schema's own description. Since GH #538 that description states the boundary as a DECISION the caller can answer by counting -- more than one lookup, any arithmetic, a plan, a comparison -- rather than as a class it has to recognise, and it says what the caller's own web tool is for; a boundary a reader has to classify moves when the window shows the work already done once. No length cap: the order asks for a length in words (GH #894) and nothing on the consult road cuts an answer. No provider envelope: the answer is {name, description, parameters}, and wrapping it in whatever a model provider wants is the caller's business, because the caller is the one that knows its provider. And no memory schema: `memory_recall` is declared by the memory hive that answers it, not here.
description.emits_meaning: schemas[]: `{name, description, parameters}` for every asked name this core serves to THIS asker's half, sorted for `*`. unknown[]: the names it does not serve to this asker, verbatim -- a name of the other half included. hop.error_code `tool_unknown` when that list is non-empty, `tools_missing` when the request carried no `tools` slot at all -- an absent list and an empty one are two different requests. hop.audience: `core` or `voice`, the half this answer carries -- the composite routes on it.
description.consumes_meaning: body.tools: the names the asking cell declares it uses, e.g. ["consult_cogny", "reply_to_consult"]. The single entry ["*"] asks for everything this core declares to the asker's half: two schemas for a voice, one (`ask_requester`) for the core itself. hop.tool_caller: who asks (see `consumes.hop`).
examples: {"tools":["*"]} from a voice -> `consult_cogny` and `reply_to_consult`, unknown empty
{"tools":["consult_cogny","web_search"]} -> one schema, unknown ["web_search"], hop.error_code `tool_unknown` -- the tools hive answers that one
{"tools":["ask_requester"]} from a voice -> no schema, unknown ["ask_requester"] -- the core's question tool is not a voice's
